fixes.explanation: Good guess, friend, because the priests do show up in this passage. But they're the ones blowing the trumpets. “The sons of Aaron, the priests, are to sound the trumpets.” (Numbers 10:8). The ones who gather when only one trumpet sounds are “…the leaders, the heads of the clans of Israel…” (Numbers 10:4). So the priests blow, and the heads of the clans gather.

Lightning shows up, flashes and is gone before you finish saying "whoa." The text says the cloud “…appeared like fire above the tabernacle from evening until morning.” Then it says the cloud “…would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire.” (Numbers 9:16). So it was there day and night, and nobody had to wait around for a flash.

Not quite, friend. The text says it remained that way continually. The cloud would cover the tabernacle by day, and at night it would appear like fire. So it wasn't a one day thing. The cloud stayed over the tabernacle.
Yes! The text says, “…wherever the cloud settled, there the Israelites would camp.” The cloud settles, and that's where the camp goes. I'd love it if my own plans were that clear.

That's right. Verse 18 says, “At the LORD’s command the Israelites set out, and at the LORD’s command they camped.” Both the going and the stopping were at His command. Verse 23 says it again: “They camped at the LORD’s command, and they set out at the LORD’s command…”

That's right. Verse 6 says, “When you sound the short blasts a second time, the camps that lie on the south side are to set out.” The first short blasts are for the camps on the east side (Numbers 10:5). The second time, it's the south side. Two rounds of short blasts, two sets of camps.

True! The LORD says, “When you enter into battle in your land against an adversary who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.” (Numbers 10:9). Notice the setting. It's battle in their land, against an adversary who attacks them. And the promise is the LORD's own word.

It's actually true, friend. Verse 9 says, “When you enter into battle in your land against an adversary who attacks you, sound short blasts on the trumpets, and you will be remembered before the LORD your God and saved from your enemies.” The setting is battle in their land, against an adversary who attacks them. The LORD is the one who makes the promise.

Yes! Verse 10 says the trumpets blown over the offerings are “…to serve as a reminder for you before your God.” The verse lists joyous occasions, appointed feasts and the beginning of each month. The burnt offerings and peace offerings are where the trumpets are blown. Silver trumpets over the offerings, now that's a way to mark a day.

The text doesn't call it a warning. Verse 10 lists joyous occasions, appointed feasts and the beginning of each month. Over the burnt offerings and peace offerings, the trumpets “…serve as a reminder for you before your God.” The word in the verse is reminder.
